name: Mount Kilimanjaro
excerpt: Kilimanjaro 7 days Machame route is highly recommended for high altitude acclimatization. The route is very scenic, providing hikers with incredible views and varying landscapes.
body:
Kilimanjaro 7 days Machame route is highly recommended for high altitude acclimatization. The route is very scenic, providing hikers with incredible views and varying landscapes. Though the climbing can be done in six days/five nights for experienced climbers, the summit success rate is significantly higher when taking the 7-day option as it will allow you sufficient time to acclimate to the altitude. The route’s length is approximately 62 km/ 37 miles from start to finish (Machame Gate to Mweka Gate). According to statistics from Kilimanjaro National Park, approximately 50% of trekkers use the Machame Route to ascend Kilimanjaro. It is designed for physically fit people with some hiking experience, though plenty of first-time trekkers have taken Machame Route and done just fine.

This tour will lead you to a village with a hidden treasure of history and culture for about 45 min drive from Kilimanjaro. This is Kibosho which is located adjacent slopes of Mount Kilimanjaro. It is home to one of the oldest Catholic Church in Tanzania. You will have an opportunity to visit a 120-year-old Kibosho Catholic Church at the foot of Mt Kilimanjaro is a stunning structure composed entirely of stones. It was built by the Germans in 1893 and is located in the midst of the banana plantations in the area. On arrival you will be given a tour of the church and the history of this magnificent building will be explained in-depth for 30 minutes. thereafter we will start a hike in amazing hills with wonderful sceneries viewing the Kibo the peak of Kilimanjaro. Here you will meet locals and learn the history of Chagga and their livelihoods. The green scenaries of the old-growth tree, coffee and banana plantations, history and culture is a rewarding experience for this tour. It is truly an unforgettable experience.

name: Serengeti National Park
excerpt: Our 7-day migration safari in Serengeti is one of the best Migration Safaris in Africa.
body:
Our 7-day migration safari in Serengeti is one of the best Migration Safaris in Africa. Safaris have been a way to discover wildlife in Tanzania for decades and the country is blessed with the winning combination of both superb game viewing and stunning tropical beaches. Welcome and experience nature in a different way.

The second dry season is December to February in which tourists can experience live birth of different species such as wildebeest. It is estimated that 500,000 calves are at Ndutu southern Serengeti. During the dry season there are few mosquitoes because there is little or no rain so less chance to be bitten, thus free from malaria. Additionally, in this season the sky is clear and most days are sunny hence it is easy to spot animals as they concentrate in the waterholes to search water services and along rivers areas. You should note that in the morning and midnight it usually gets cold so visitors are recommended to have warm clothing.

The great migration one of the world’s most spectacular wildlife events, the Great Migration, occurs during the high season. Millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles move across the Serengeti Plains in search of fresh grazing grounds. Witnessing the dramatic river crossings, particularly at the Mara River, is a once-in-a-lifetime experience.

name: Ngorongoro Crater
excerpt: The Ngorongoro Conservation Area is a protected area and a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in Ngorongoro District, 180 km (110 mi) west of Arusha City in the Arusha Region, within the Crater Highlands geological area of northern Tanzania.
body:
The Ngorongoro Conservation Area is a protected area and a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in Ngorongoro District, 180 km (110 mi) west of Arusha City in the Arusha Region, within the Crater Highlands geological area of northern Tanzania. The area is named after Ngorongoro Crater, a large volcanic caldera within the area. The Ngorongoro Conservation Area Authority administers the conservation area, an arm of the Tanzanian government, and its boundaries follow the boundary of the Ngorongoro District in the Arusha Region. The western portion of the park abuts the Serengeti National Park, and the area comprising the two parks and Kenya’s Maasai Mara game reserve is home to Great Migration, a massive annual migration of millions of wildebeest, zebras, gazelles, and other animals. The conservation area also contains Olduvai Gorge, one of the most important paleoanthropological sites in the world.

name: Tarangire National Park
excerpt: Tarangire National Park contains a variety of wildlife, both big and small. The park is popular for the high elephant population; you may see them roaming around in the bush searching for food and relaxation.
body: Tarangire National Park contains a variety of wildlife, both big and small. The park is popular for the high elephant population; you may see them roaming around in the bush searching for food and relaxation. During the dry season, see them heading to the river just enjoying the pure drinks and cooling themselves from the hot sun during the daytime. The park also contains over 500 bird species and a beautiful landscape nourished with baobab trees that stand as towers in the savannah land. These ancient baobab trees play a vital role in ecosystems used as habitat for bees, birds, and bats. Also, they have beautiful fruits and store water, hence providing support during the dry season.

name: Arusha & Mount Meru
excerpt: At a height of 4,566 meters (14,980 ft), Mount Meru is a dormant stratovolcano located in Arusha National Park, 70 Kilometres (43 miles) west of Mount Kilimanjaro in the country of Tanzania.
body:
At a height of 4,566 meters (14,980 ft), Mount Meru is a dormant stratovolcano located in Arusha National Park, 70 Kilometres (43 miles) west of Mount Kilimanjaro in the country of Tanzania. Typically Mount Meru Climb takes four days, but it can be done in 3 days to complete a trek to the Summit.

This tour will lead you to the hidden treasure outside Arusha City .Exploring the Napuru waterfalls of Mount Meru stands out as one of our cherished offerings in Arusha. Situated adjacent to Arusha National Park, Mount Meru claims the second-highest peak in Tanzania following Mount Kilimanjaro. This dormant volcano boasts rich, fertile slopes, nurturing an array of stunning flora and fauna along the path to the waterfall. Guided by an English-speaking expert, the hike to the fall’s spans 30 minutes. Post-tour, you’ll have the chance to immerse yourself in a coffee farm visit, gaining firsthand knowledge in the art of crafting a cup of coffee. The experience culminates in a delightful tasting session, promising to leave a lasting impression. Later you will go drive back to your hotel revitalized and relaxed full of memories of the landscapes.

Our driver guide will pick you at your hotel at 9:00am and start your journey to the Olpopongi Maasai Village. The Olpopongi Maasai-Village is located in West Kilimanjaro 74 kilometers from Kilimanjaro and 85 kilometers from Arusha accessible for visitors from both Kilimanjaro and Arusha. The village was planned and built by a multi-cultural construction team, led by more than 50 Maasai women & men from the nearby Tinga-Tinga Maasai-Village. All houses are built the traditional way with local and natural materials only, similar to those ones of the nearby Maasai people. The income obtained from your tour supports local Maasai families with water, food, employment, personal income, medical treatments and education. Activities include a village tour, lesson on hunting techniques, demonstration of traditional medicine and bush walk in the Maasai land of the village. A traditional lunch is also served. A traditional lunch will be prepared for you in the afternoon. After your tour of the village, you will be transferred back to your hotel in Kilimanjaro or Arusha

name: Zanzibar
excerpt: A spice farm tour in Zanzibar is a unique, immersive experience that delves into the island’s rich history as a spice hub and offers a sensory exploration of its agricultural treasures.
body:
A spice farm tour in Zanzibar is a unique, immersive experience that delves into the island’s rich history as a spice hub and offers a sensory exploration of its agricultural treasures. Known as the “Spice Island,” Zanzibar has a tropical climate ideal for cultivating a variety of spices such as cloves, cinnamon, black pepper, cardamom, nutmeg, and vanilla. These spices, which once drove Zanzibar’s economy and established its historical significance on the trade routes, remain an integral part of the island’s identity and local culture. Our guide will meet you and after introductions you will depart for the tour. In this tour our knowledgeable guide will clarify to you why Zanzibar is called Spice Island. The tour will be in a small plantation whereby you’ll see where spices grow, among them cloves, nutmeg, vanilla, Zanzibar’s cardamoms, cinnamon, curry, menthol, pepper, tamarind, and ginger. Many of the spices are truly beautiful to behold, and rarely does the leaf or berry visually resemble what’s on your spice rack at home. Depending on the season, you may see, smell and sometimes taste between 25-50 different spices, fruits and other plants. Your guide will give detailed descriptions of what each plant is used for, and not all are for food. In this tour you will have an opportunity to visit the spice shop on the farm, where you can buy fresh spices to use in your cooking at home. The spices will make a truly memory of your holiday in Zanzibar.

The Nakupenda Beach tour in Zanzibar offers visitors a slice of paradise, with stunning white sands, crystal-clear turquoise waters, and a tranquil, tropical ambiance. Nakupenda, meaning “I love you” in Swahili, is a pristine sandbank located just off the coast of Stone Town. Accessible only by boat, the sandbank appears and disappears with the tides, creating a unique, ephemeral setting ideal for a day trip filled with relaxation, swimming, and marine exploration. It is a very particular island, quite typical of the zone, with white sand, clean water. You will visit prison island first on boat, with the giant tortoises, and learn about culture and history. Later you will reach a sand bank at Nakupenda and whilst you do snorkel and other beach activities, we will prepare an excellent meal (a sea food taste) with fresh fruits. Nakupenda is located about 20 minutes on boat from stone Town’s coast and it is a big dune of sand which get submerged during the high tide and is a great place to rest, get tan, enjoy the water and relax. This tour suits all groups solo, couples, family and big groups. Relax on the sandbank or discover marine life around the sandbank before riding our motorboat or sailing back to Stone town.

Prison island Is a small, picturesque island located about 5.6 kilometres (3.5 miles) northwest of Stone Town, Zanzibar. This coral island is a popular tourist destination, known for its intriguing history, stunning beaches, and its sanctuary of giant Aldabra tortoises. You will have an opportunity to explore the rich culture and history of Zanzibar with a visit to Prison Island by boat. See the large tortoises that inhabit the Island, and enjoy the opportunity to snorkel off the coast. You will visit Prison Island on a private 3-hour tour, and discover the rich history and beautiful natural surroundings of this location. Meet your guide in Zanzibar, or select the option including hotel pickup, then enjoy the ride to the island on a traditional dhow. Learn how this small island gained its name and explore the place that is now home to more than 50 tortoises, some over 100 years old. You will also have another experience of feeding the tortoises and take up-close pictures with them, as you keep a lookout for the peacocks and antelope that also live there. After discovering the island and its history, take the opportunity to snorkel in the clear waters off the coast amongst tropical fish and colourful coral. At the end of your tour, you will return to Stone town, where you’ll be dropped off in the city centre, or at your hotel. Hotel pick-up and drop off from Stone Town hotels is free, however, transfers from beach hotels, Zanzibar Port and Airport can be booked at small additional cost.

name: Lake Victoria
excerpt: Saanane Island offers breathtaking views of Lake Victoria, surrounding islands, lush greenery, and fascinating rock formations.
body:
Saanane Island offers breathtaking views of Lake Victoria, surrounding islands, lush greenery, and fascinating rock formations. It is the perfect destination for game viewing, birdwatching, rock hiking, boat cruises, nature walks, picnics, bush lunches, photography, meditation, and sport fishing. The island is home to diverse wildlife, including impalas, zebras, crocodiles, lizards, hyraxes, and over 200 recorded bird species.

Saanane Island is easily accessible via a short 5-minute boat ride from the park offices on the mainland. The park offices are just a 15-minute walk from the Mwanza city center.
